status_summary: On 2026-09-17 the SEC issued an Innovation Exemption order giving temporary, conditional exemptions for five years to venues trading tokenized stocks and to liquidity providers, which the Chairman's statement ties to the Exchange Act general exemptive authority in section 36(a)(1); it relieves trading venues rather than issuers. On 2026-08-21 the SEC published proposed Regulation Crypto Assets, with issuer offering exemptions of $5 million over four years and $75 million per 12 months, comments due 2026-10-20. The issuer-focused step is a proposal, and no measure showing more frequent use of exemptive authority was found.

timeline.event: The SEC publishes the proposed Regulation Crypto Assets, with offering exemptions of $5 million over four years and $75 million per 12 months and a conditional safe harbor; comments are due 2026-10-20.

The SEC issues an order under Exchange Act section 36(a)(1) granting temporary, conditional exemptions from the exchange and dealer definitions for tokenized securities venues and liquidity providers, expiring five years after publication, and invites comment.

title: Use SEC general exemptive authority more often to reduce burdens on issuers
uncertainties: Exemptive orders issued in 2025 were not itemized; a March 2025 law-firm note describing several orders was paywalled.
